claims.text: A contract test checks one side of an integration against a shared description of what the other side expects; a consumer-driven contract is written by the consumer, lists only what it reads, and the provider tests against it.

Listing only the fields the app reads lets the API add fields freely and fails only changes the app would notice; listing every field fails harmless changes, and the team can drift into editing samples until green.

claims.text: The contract checks shape, not meaning: a priceVnd sent in thousands would pass both tests; review still has to catch such changes.

To add a field the API adds it first, then the app adds it to fromJson and the sample together; to rename, the API sends both names, the app moves, then the API drops the old one; a second client gets its own samples and API-side test.
